examples.ko: 우리 수업이 아침 아홉 시에 시작돼요.
examples.en: Our class starts at nine in the morning.

examples.ko: 우리가 도착했을 때 영화가 벌써 시작됐어요.
examples.en: The movie had already started when we arrived.
The new semester will start tomorrow.
Before the game starts, the players greet each other.
The meeting started, so I turned off my phone.

examples.ko: 방학이 시작되면 가족과 여행을 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: When vacation starts, I want to travel with my family.

explain: '시작하다'는 사람이 일을 여는 것이고, '시작되다'는 시간이 되어 저절로 열리는 것이에요. 수업·영화·회의·방학처럼 주어가 사람이 아닌 일일 때 '시작되다'를 써요. 짝말로 '이야기가 시작되다', '새로운 하루가 시작되다'도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '시작하다' is for a person who starts something; '시작되다' is for something that starts on its own when the time comes. Use it when the subject is an event, not a person: class, a movie, a meeting, vacation. Common phrases include 'a new day begins' and 'the story begins'.

examples.en: In summer the rain goes on for over a week.
The meeting went on for three hours.

examples.ko: 이 더위는 다음 주에도 계속될 거예요.
examples.en: This heat will continue next week too.
I'm so tired from the nonstop overtime.
My cough kept going for days, so I went to the hospital.
The two people's conversation continued until night.

explain: '계속하다'는 사람이 이어 가는 것이고, '계속되다'는 일이 저절로 이어지는 것이에요. 비·더위·기침·야근처럼 내가 멈추기 어려운 일에 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '계속 공부해요'처럼 '계속'만 부사로 붙여 쓰는 경우가 훨씬 많아요.
explain_en: '계속하다' is when a person keeps something going; '계속되다' is when something just keeps going by itself. It fits things you can't easily stop: rain, heat, a cough, overtime. In everyday speech, '계속' alone as an adverb ('계속 공부해요') is far more common.

examples.ko: 아버지는 이십 년 동안 중학교 선생으로 일하셨어요.
examples.en: My father worked as a middle school teacher for twenty years.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 피아노 선생한테 배웠어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I learned from a piano teacher.
He is a math teacher, so he calculates fast.

examples.ko: 새로 온 영어 선생을 만나 봤어요?
examples.en: Have you met the new English teacher?

examples.ko: 이 학교에는 선생이 모두 열 명이에요.
examples.en: This school has ten teachers in total.
My dream is to be an elementary school teacher.

explain: 사람을 부르거나 높일 때는 '선생' 대신 '선생님'이라고 해요. '선생'만 쓰면 직업을 말하거나 제3자를 가리키는 느낌이 강하고, 앞에 있는 선생님께 쓰면 높임이 부족해요. 반대말(짝말)은 '학생'이에요.
explain_en: When you address or honor a teacher, say '선생님', not '선생'. Bare '선생' sounds like naming the job or referring to a third person, and it falls short of respect to a teacher in front of you. Its counterpart is '학생'.

examples.ko: 부모님은 저를 어릴 때부터 열심히 공부시켰어요.
examples.en: My parents made me study hard from when I was little.
Mom makes my younger sibling study in a quiet room.
The parents sent the child to a cram school to get them studying.
If you force a child to study, they dislike studying.

examples.ko: 우리 아빠는 저를 공부시킨 뒤에 놀아도 된다고 했어요.
examples.en: My dad said I could play after making me study.

examples.ko: 선생님이 오늘 학생들을 다 같이 공부시킬 거예요.
examples.en: The teacher will have all the students study together today.

explain: '공부하다'는 내가 직접 하는 것이고, '공부시키다'는 아이나 학생이 공부하게 만드는 것이에요. 주어는 보통 부모나 선생님이고, 공부하는 사람에게는 '을/를'을 붙여요. '공부를 시키다'처럼 띄어 써도 같아요.
explain_en: '공부하다' is studying yourself; '공부시키다' is making a child or student study. The subject is usually a parent or teacher, and the person studying takes the object particle. Writing it as '공부를 시키다' means the same thing.

examples.en: A famous band came to our school.
I play guitar in the school band.
I often listen to this band's songs.
My older brother started a new band with his friends.
Do you want to go see a band concert this weekend?
That band is really popular.

explain: 노래만 하는 팀은 '그룹', 악기를 직접 연주하는 팀은 '밴드'라고 구분하는 경우가 많아요. 상처에 붙이는 '밴드'(반창고)도 소리가 같아서 앞뒤 말을 보고 알아야 해요.
explain_en: A team that only sings is often called a '그룹', while one that plays instruments is a '밴드'. An adhesive bandage is also called '밴드' in Korean, so use the context to tell them apart.

examples.en: I bought a pink bag.
A light pink suits my younger sibling well.

examples.ko: 공원이 벚꽃 때문에 온통 핑크로 보여요.
examples.en: The park looks all pink because of the cherry blossoms.
This pink is so strong that it feels like too much.
I tried wearing pink and white together.
Strawberry milk is cute because it is a pretty pink.

explain: 같은 색을 '분홍색'이라고도 해요. '핑크'는 외래어라 옷·화장품·가게 이름처럼 세련된 느낌을 줄 때 많이 쓰고, 일상에서는 둘 다 자연스러워요. 뒤에 '색'을 붙여 '핑크색'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 두 사람 사이에 핑크빛 기류가 흘러요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분홍색이라는 뜻이 아니라 연애가 시작될 것 같은 설렘이나 밝은 전망을 말해요. '핑크빛 미래'처럼도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not about the color itself: it suggests budding romance or a bright outlook, as in '핑크빛 미래' (a rosy future).

explain_en: The same color is also called '분홍색'. '핑크' is a loanword, common for clothes, cosmetics and shop names where a trendy feel is wanted; both are natural in daily speech. You can add '색' to say '핑크색'.

examples.ko: 이 경험이 나중에 플러스가 될 거예요.
examples.en: This experience will be a plus later.
Being good at English is a big plus for getting a job.
In math class I learned that 3 plus 2 is 5.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 무료지만 플러스 버전은 더 편해요.
examples.en: This app is free, but the Plus version is more convenient.
A cheerful personality is a big plus too.

examples.ko: 마이너스 말고 플러스가 되는 점을 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's think about the plus side, not the minus.

explain: 반대말은 '마이너스'예요. 계산과 온도에서는 '더하기'·'영상'처럼 한국어 말도 쓰지만, '이득이 되다'라는 뜻으로는 '플러스'가 거의 굳어 있어요. 앱이나 서비스 이름에 붙으면 '더 좋은 유료판'이라는 느낌을 줘요.

phrases.example: 이 경험이 나중에 플러스가 될 거예요.
phrases.en: to work in your favor; to count as a plus
phrases.nuance_ko: 계산이 아니라 이득·도움이 된다는 뜻이에요. 반대는 '마이너스가 되다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not arithmetic: it means something helps or benefits you. The opposite is '마이너스가 되다'.

explain_en: The opposite is '마이너스'. For math and temperature there are Korean words like '더하기' and '영상', but for 'a benefit' the loanword '플러스' is almost fixed. Added to an app or service name, it suggests a better paid version.

en: cheer up; keep your spirits up; hang in there

examples.ko: 조금만 더 힘내요, 거의 다 왔어요!
examples.en: Hang in there a little more, we're almost there!
A friend said 'Hang in there!' to me.
Let's keep it up and run all the way to the end.
I got my energy back after being cheered on.
The way you keep trying until the end is really cool.
I'll give it more effort in the next game.

explain: 응원할 때 가장 흔한 말이에요. 친구에게는 '힘내', 어른에게는 '힘내세요'라고 해요. '파이팅'과 함께 쓰는 경우가 많고, '힘을 내다'로 띄어 써도 같아요. 아주 슬픈 사람에게는 '힘내'라는 말이 부담이 될 수 있어서 '많이 힘들었죠' 같은 말을 먼저 하기도 해요.
explain_en: This is the most common way to cheer someone on. Use '힘내' with friends and '힘내세요' with elders. It often pairs with '파이팅', and '힘을 내다' written separately means the same. To someone who is very sad, '힘내' can feel like pressure, so Koreans sometimes start with something like 'That must have been hard.'

examples.en: My favorite color is purple.
Purple flowers bloomed all along the road.

examples.ko: 동생은 보라 원피스를 입고 파티에 갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sister went to the party in a purple dress.

examples.ko: 해 질 무렵 하늘이 보라로 물들었어요.
examples.en: At sunset the sky turned purple.
Grape juice is pretty because it has a deep purple hue.
Purple and yellow go well together.

explain: 색 이름으로는 '보라'보다 '보라색'이라고 더 많이 말해요. 같은 소리의 '보라'는 '보다'의 명령형('보라고 했어요')이기도 해서 문장 속에서 구분해야 해요. 붉은 기가 더 강한 보라는 '자주색'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: For the color, people say '보라색' more often than bare '보라'. The same sound is also a command form of '보다' ('보라고 했어요'), so you tell them apart in the sentence. A more reddish purple is called '자주색'.

examples.en: On my birthday my friends bought me a cake.
It always rains on my birthday.
On my birthday I had dinner with my family.
My mom's birthday is April 20th.
Since it is my birthday, I left work early today.
I wrote my friend's birthday on the calendar.

explain: 그냥 '생일'이 훨씬 흔하고, '생일날'은 생일 바로 그날을 강조할 때 써요. '생일 선물', '생일 파티'처럼 합쳐진 말에는 '생일'을 써요. 어른의 생일은 높여서 '생신'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Plain '생일' is far more common; '생일날' stresses the actual day itself. In compounds like 'birthday gift' and 'birthday party', use '생일'. An elder's birthday is honored as '생신'.

en: seem; be thought; appear to one

examples.en: This problem seems very hard to me.
At first that job seemed easy to me.

examples.ko: 오늘은 비가 올 것 같다고 생각돼서 우산을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I thought it might rain today, so I packed an umbrella.

examples.ko: 이 방법이 가장 좋다고 생각되는 이유가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a reason this method seems best to me.

examples.ko: 다음 주에는 모든 게 달라질 거라고 생각되지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't think everything will change next week.
If it seems that way to you, please tell me honestly.

explain: '생각하다'는 내가 생각을 만드는 것이고, '생각되다'는 그렇게 느껴진다는 부드러운 표현이에요. 발표나 보고서에서 의견을 조심스럽게 말할 때 '-다고 생각돼요/생각됩니다'를 자주 써요. '생각나다'(떠오르다)와는 달라요.
explain_en: '생각하다' is you forming a thought; '생각되다' is a softer way to say it comes across that way. In presentations and reports, '-다고 생각돼요/생각됩니다' is common for stating an opinion carefully. It is different from '생각나다' (to come to mind).

examples.en: This app is used all over the world.
This room used to be used as a meeting room.

examples.ko: 이 도구는 요리할 때만 사용되는 것이 아니에요.
examples.en: This tool isn't used only when cooking.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 편지에서 자주 사용돼서 알아 두면 좋아요.
examples.en: This word is often used in letters, so it's good to know.

examples.ko: 앞으로 이 건물은 도서관으로 사용될 거예요.
examples.en: From now on, this building will be used as a library.

examples.ko: 버려지지 않고 다시 사용되면 환경에 좋아요.
examples.en: If things are reused instead of thrown away, it's good for the environment.

explain: '사용하다'는 사람이 쓰는 것이고, '사용되다'는 쓰이는 물건이나 말이 주어예요. 설명서·뉴스·보고서에서 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '쓰여요'(쓰이다)를 더 많이 써요. 도구·말·돈에는 '사용', 시설·서비스에는 '이용'이 어울려요.
explain_en: '사용하다' is a person using something; with '사용되다' the thing or word being used is the subject. You see it in manuals, news and reports. In speech, '쓰여요' (쓰이다) is more common. Use '사용' for tools, words and money, and '이용' for facilities and services.

examples.en: This drama airs every Saturday.
That news was broadcast nationwide yesterday.

examples.ko: 새 예능 프로그램이 다음 달부터 방송될 거예요.
examples.en: The new variety show will start airing next month.
I drive while listening to music broadcast on the radio.
This scene was cut before it aired.
The final episode aired and everyone cried.

explain: '방송하다'는 만드는 쪽이 내보내는 것이고, '방송되다'는 프로그램이 나가는 것이에요. TV 드라마는 '방영되다'라고도 하는데, '방송되다'는 라디오 같은 소리 방송에도 써요. 말로는 '몇 시에 해요?'처럼 '하다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: '방송하다' is the side that sends it out; '방송되다' is the program going out. TV dramas can also be '방영되다', but '방송되다' works for audio broadcasts like radio too. In speech, people often just say '몇 시에 해요?' with '하다'.

en: proceed; be carried out; go on

examples.en: The meeting is going well as planned.
The road construction is moving very slowly.
The event was held starting at two in the afternoon.
If the class is conducted in English, it's hard to understand.
I am glad everything went smoothly.
Tomorrow's interview will be held online.

explain: '진행하다'는 사람이 이끌고, '진행되다'는 일이 정해진 절차대로 흘러가는 것이에요. 회의·행사·공사·수업·인터뷰처럼 순서가 있는 일에 써요. '잘 진행되다', '순조롭게 진행되다'가 자주 나오는 짝이에요.
explain_en: '진행하다' is a person leading something; '진행되다' is an event moving along through its set steps. Use it for things with an order: meetings, events, construction, classes, interviews. '잘 진행되다' and '순조롭게 진행되다' are common pairings.

examples.en: Dinner is all ready on the table.
The presentation materials are already prepared.

examples.ko: 모든 것이 다 준비되면 바로 출발해요.
examples.en: Let us leave right away once everything is ready.

examples.ko: 이불과 베개가 손님 방에 준비되어 있어요.
examples.en: Blankets and pillows are ready in the guest room.
Please call me as soon as the food is ready.
The gifts will all be ready by tomorrow.

explain: '준비하다'는 내가 하는 일이고, '준비되다'는 끝나서 갖춰진 상태예요. '준비됐어요?'는 '다 됐어요?'라는 뜻으로 일상에서 자주 물어요. '준비가 되다'로 풀어 쓰는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: '준비하다' is the act of preparing; '준비되다' is the state of being all set. '준비됐어요?' is a very common everyday question, like asking 'all set?' It is also often split up as '준비가 되다'.

en: be confirmed; be verified; be checked

examples.en: The cause of the accident hasn't been confirmed yet.
The name and address on the application have both been verified.
When the reservation is confirmed, I'll send you a text.
An error was found, so we fixed the app again.
The news says a new fact has been confirmed.
I'll tell you as soon as it's confirmed.

explain: '확인하다'는 내가 맞는지 보는 것이고, '확인되다'는 확인한 결과가 나온 상태예요. 뉴스·공지·보고서에서 '~로 확인됐다'라는 표현을 자주 봐요. 아직이면 '확인되지 않았어요', 또는 '미확인'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '확인하다' is you checking whether something is right; '확인되다' is the state after the result comes out. News, notices and reports often say '~로 확인됐다'. If it is not done yet, say '확인되지 않았어요' or use '미확인'.

examples.en: This trip was planned a very long time ago.
The park construction is planned for next year.
We set off according to the planned schedule.

examples.ko: 모임이 계획되면 단체 채팅방에 알려 줄게요.
examples.en: When a get-together is planned, I'll tell you in the group chat.

examples.ko: 새 지하철역이 이 지역에 계획되고 있어요.
examples.en: A new subway station is being planned for this area.
The event that was first planned was suddenly canceled.

explain: '계획하다'는 사람이 세우는 것이고, '계획되다'는 어떤 일이 이미 계획 안에 들어 있는 상태예요. 공사·행사·일정처럼 큰 일에 잘 쓰고, 개인 이야기는 '계획이 있어요'나 '계획을 세웠어요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '계획하다' is a person making a plan; '계획되다' is something already being in the plan. It suits bigger things like construction, events and schedules. For personal talk, '계획이 있어요' or '계획을 세웠어요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The company trains new employees for three months.

examples.ko: 부모는 아이를 바르게 교육시키고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: Parents want to bring their child up properly.

examples.ko: 학교는 모든 학생을 안전하게 지내도록 교육시켰어요.
examples.en: The school educated all the students to stay safe.
This center plans to train foreigners.

examples.ko: 새 요리사를 교육시키려면 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Training a new cook takes a long time.
Educating children is not easy.

explain: '교육하다'는 가르치는 일 자체이고, '교육시키다'는 누군가를 교육받게 하는 것이에요. 회사 연수나 공식적인 글에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '가르치다'가 훨씬 흔해요. 동물에게는 '훈련시키다'가 더 어울려요.
explain_en: '교육하다' is the act of teaching; '교육시키다' is making someone receive education. It appears in company training and formal writing, while everyday speech uses '가르치다' far more. For animals, '훈련시키다' fits better.

examples.en: The meeting date hasn't been decided yet.
The wedding venue was decided at today's meeting.
The representative is decided by a vote.
Once the price is decided, I'll let you know right away.
There is one thing that will be decided today.
The exam date was set, so I started studying.

explain: '결정하다'는 내가 정하는 것이고, '결정되다'는 결과로 정해진 상태예요. 말할 때는 '정해지다'가 더 자주 들리고, '결정되다'는 뉴스·공지·회의처럼 공식적인 자리에서 많이 써요.
explain_en: '결정하다' is you deciding; '결정되다' is the state of having been settled. In speech '정해지다' is heard more, while '결정되다' is common in news, notices and meetings.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 제 일과 관계되지 않아요.
examples.en: This problem isn't related to my work.
I looked up information related to health on the internet.

examples.ko: 이 일에 관계된 사람은 모두 모였어요.
examples.en: Everyone involved in this matter gathered.

examples.ko: 이 두 일이 서로 관계돼 있다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard these two things are connected to each other.

examples.ko: 그 사건과 관계되면 조사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: If you're connected to that case, you have to be questioned.
I'm worried because this matter is connected to money.

explain: 일상에서는 '관계가 있어요/관계없어요'가 훨씬 많이 쓰여요. '관계되다'는 '~와 관계되는 일', '관계된 사람'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 나와요. '관련되다'도 비슷한데 뉴스와 글에서 더 흔해요.
explain_en: In daily life, '관계가 있어요' and '관계없어요' are much more common. '관계되다' often shows up modifying a noun, as in '~와 관계되는 일' or '관계된 사람'. '관련되다' is similar and more common in news and writing.

en: be used (by someone for their own gain); be exploited

examples.ko: 저는 친구에게 이용당한 것 같아서 슬퍼요.
examples.en: I feel sad because it seems my friend used me.

examples.ko: 그는 사람들에게 이용당해도 화를 내지 않았어요.
examples.en: He didn't get angry even when people used him.
If you do not want to be used by others, refuse clearly.
Very naive people get used easily.
I felt the company was using me, so I quit my job.
I read contracts carefully so I won't be taken advantage of.

explain: 남이 자기 이익을 위해 나를 쓴 불쾌한 경험을 말해요. 단순히 서비스를 쓰는 '이용하다'나 중립적인 '이용되다'와 달라요. '무시당하다', '사기당하다'처럼 '-당하다'가 붙은 말은 보통 나쁜 일에 써요.
explain_en: It describes the unpleasant experience of being used by someone for their own benefit. It differs from plain '이용하다' (using a service) and the neutral '이용되다'. Verbs ending in '-당하다', like '무시당하다' and '사기당하다', are normally used for bad things.

examples.en: This building is used as a student lounge.
This transit card is used nationwide.
The leftover ingredients were used in another dish too.

examples.ko: 이 기술은 병원에서도 이용될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This technology can be used in hospitals too.
The longer it is used, the more the fee goes up.

examples.ko: 휴일에는 이 주차장이 무료로 이용되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish this parking lot could be used for free on holidays.

explain: '이용'은 시설·서비스·교통·자원을 활용하는 느낌이고, '사용'은 펜·단어·돈처럼 물건을 쓰는 느낌이에요. 도서관·지하철은 '이용', 펜·단어는 '사용'이 어울려요. 사람을 자기 이익으로 쓰면 '이용당하다'로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: '이용' has the feel of making use of facilities, services, transport or resources, while '사용' is using objects like a pen, a word or money. A library or subway is '이용'; a pen or a word is '사용'. When a person is used for someone's gain, it becomes '이용당하다'.

en: be made public; be released; be revealed

examples.en: The trailer for the new movie was released yesterday.
The exam results will be made public next week.
Personal information must not be made public.
I was shocked that the secret photo was posted online.
Everyone is waiting for the day it's revealed.

examples.ko: 새 제품은 내년 봄에 공개될 거예요.
examples.en: The new product will be unveiled next spring.

explain: '공개하다'는 내보이는 쪽, '공개되다'는 숨겨져 있던 것이 보이게 되는 쪽이에요. 반대말은 '비공개'예요. 영화·제품·정보·사진에 두루 쓰고, 구어에서는 '오픈되다'도 들려요. '발표되다'는 공식적으로 알린다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: '공개하다' is showing it; '공개되다' is something hidden coming into view. The opposite is '비공개'. It works for movies, products, information and photos, and in casual speech you may hear '오픈되다' too. '발표되다' has a stronger feel of an official announcement.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 한국의 작은 회사에서 개발됐어요.
examples.en: This app was developed by a small company in Korea.
A new vaccine is being developed quickly.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 앞으로 크게 개발될 거예요.
examples.en: This area will be developed on a large scale.

examples.ko: 개발된 지 얼마 안 된 기술이에요.
examples.en: It's a technology that was developed not long ago.
When new technology is developed, life gets easier.
A new drug was developed, and the patients are happy.

explain: 기술·제품·약처럼 새로 만들어질 때도, 땅이 새 도시나 단지가 될 때도 '개발되다'를 써요. 사람이 주어이면 '개발하다'예요. 이미 있는 것이 더 좋아질 때는 '발전하다'나 '발달하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Use '개발되다' both when a technology, product or drug is newly created and when land is turned into a new town or complex. With a person as the subject, it becomes '개발하다'. For something that already exists and improves, '발전하다' or '발달하다' fits better.

examples.en: What happened that day will be remembered for a long time.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 일이 아직도 또렷하게 기억돼요.
examples.en: Things from my childhood are still vivid in my memory.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 좋은 선생으로 기억되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: He wants to be remembered as a good teacher.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 많은 사람에게 기억되는 노래를 남겼어요.
examples.en: That singer left behind a song many people remember.
This event has to be remembered in history.

examples.ko: 제 이름이 사람들에게 좋게 기억되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope my name will be remembered well by people.

explain: '기억하다'는 내가 기억하는 것이고, '기억되다'는 사람들 마음에 남는 것이에요. '기억나다'는 갑자기 떠오르는 것이라 또 달라요. 일상에서는 '기억나요'나 '기억에 남아요'가 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: '기억하다' is you remembering; '기억되다' is staying in people's minds. '기억나다' is a memory suddenly coming back, which is different again. In daily speech '기억나요' and '기억에 남아요' are heard more.

examples.en: The exam results will be announced tomorrow morning.
The new song was officially released yesterday.
The successful applicants will be announced next week.
Everyone was surprised at what was announced yesterday.

examples.ko: 새 소식이 발표되면 문자로 알려 줄게요.
examples.en: When the news is announced, I'll tell you by text.

examples.ko: 연구 결과가 신문에 발표돼서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The research results were published in the newspaper and became a hot topic.

explain: '발표하다'는 사람이 앞에서 말하거나 공식으로 알리는 것이고, '발표되다'는 결과·소식이 알려지는 것이에요. 시험 결과, 신곡, 연구, 합격자처럼 공식적으로 알리는 일에 써요. 숨겨진 것을 보이게 하는 '공개되다'와 조금 달라요.
explain_en: '발표하다' is a person presenting in front of others or announcing officially; '발표되다' is a result or news becoming known. Use it for official things: exam results, new songs, research, successful applicants. It differs a little from '공개되다', which is about revealing something hidden.

examples.en: After hearing the teacher's explanation, I get it now.

examples.ko: 이 문장은 아무리 읽어도 이해되지 않아요.
examples.en: No matter how many times I read this sentence, it doesn't make sense.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 행동이 이해되면 화가 풀릴 거예요.
examples.en: Once his behavior makes sense, your anger will ease.

examples.ko: 이제야 그때 왜 화를 냈는지 이해됐어요.
examples.en: Only now do I understand why he got angry then.
Start by reading the parts that make sense to you.

examples.ko: 한국에 살아 보니 그 말이 이해돼서 웃었어요.
examples.en: After living in Korea, that phrase made sense and I laughed.

explain: '이해하다'는 내가 노력해서 알게 되는 것이고, '이해되다'는 저절로 알게 되는 것이에요. '이해가 안 돼요', '이해가 돼요'라고 말하는 경우가 가장 많아요. '그 마음이 이해돼요'처럼 사람의 마음에 공감할 때도 써요.
explain_en: '이해하다' is understanding through your own effort; '이해되다' is understanding that comes by itself. '이해가 안 돼요' and '이해가 돼요' are the most common ways to say it. It also expresses empathy, as in '그 마음이 이해돼요'.

examples.en: It's hard to make a young child understand the rules.

examples.ko: 저는 부모님을 이해시켜서 유학을 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to get my parents to understand and go study abroad.
I even drew a picture to make my friend understand.
Can I make them understand my position?

examples.ko: 한 시간 동안 설명해서 겨우 이해시켰어요.
examples.en: After explaining for an hour, I barely got them to understand.
Getting adults to understand is the hardest part.

explain: 상대가 알아듣도록 설명해서 받아들이게 만들 때 써요. '설득하다'와 달라서, 이해시키는 것은 알게 하는 것이고 설득하는 것은 생각이나 행동을 바꾸게 하는 것이에요. 설명하는 사람이 노력해야 한다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when you explain so that the other person grasps something. It differs from '설득하다': '이해시키다' is getting someone to understand, while '설득하다' is getting them to change their mind or action. It carries a feel that the explainer has to put in effort.

examples.en: This school is run with government support.
Until last year this library operated only on weekdays.

examples.ko: 이 카페는 아침 일곱 시부터 운영되고 있어요.
examples.en: This cafe is open for business from seven in the morning.

examples.ko: 잘 운영되는 가게는 손님이 계속 와요.
examples.en: A well-run shop keeps getting customers.

examples.ko: 이 모임은 회비로 운영돼서 따로 돈을 내요.
examples.en: This group is run on membership fees, so we pay separately.

examples.ko: 규칙이 없으면 회사가 제대로 운영될 수 없어요.
examples.en: Without rules, a company can't be run properly.

explain: '운영하다'는 가게·회사·학교·서비스를 꾸려 가는 사람 쪽이고, '운영되다'는 그렇게 굴러가는 상태예요. 도서관·학교·공공시설은 '운영 시간', 가게는 '영업 시간'을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: '운영하다' is the person running a shop, company, school or service; '운영되다' is the state of it running. For libraries, schools and public facilities, '운영 시간' is common, while shops more often say '영업 시간'.

examples.en: The cause of the accident is still being investigated.
This case has been under investigation since yesterday.

examples.ko: 조사된 결과를 보면 학생이 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: According to the survey results, the number of students dropped a lot.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 다음 달에 자세히 조사될 거예요.
examples.en: This issue will be looked into in detail next month.
Once people's opinions are surveyed, we'll decide then.

examples.ko: 이 병은 아직 원인이 조사되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The cause of this disease hasn't been investigated yet.

explain: '조사하다'는 사람이 살펴보는 것이고, '조사되다'는 조사의 대상이 되어 결과가 나오는 것이에요. 사고·사건 조사와 설문 조사에 모두 써요. 한국어 문법의 '조사'(을/를, 이/가)와 소리가 같아서 앞뒤 말을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: '조사하다' is a person looking into something; '조사되다' is being the subject of an investigation or survey and having results come out. It covers both accident or case investigations and opinion surveys. The same sound is also the grammar term '조사' (particles like 을/를, 이/가), so tell them apart by context.

examples.ko: 이 노래가 우리 반 대표곡으로 선택됐어요.
examples.en: This song was chosen as our class signature song.

examples.ko: 최종 후보 세 명 중 한 명이 선택돼요.
examples.en: One of the three final candidates will be chosen.

examples.ko: 이번에 선택되지 않아도 다음 기회가 있어요.
examples.en: Even if you're not chosen this time, there's another chance.

examples.ko: 학생 대표로 선택되면 인사를 해야 해요.
examples.en: If you're chosen as the student representative, you have to give a speech.
A menu that has been selected can't be changed.

examples.ko: 제 그림이 전시회에 선택될 거라고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard my painting will be chosen for the exhibition.

explain: '선택하다'는 내가 고르는 것이고, '선택되다'는 골라 주는 쪽에서 뽑아 준 상태예요. 사람이 뽑힐 때는 구어에서 '뽑히다'가 더 자연스러워요. 앱 화면에서는 '선택됨'이라는 표시로 자주 만나요.
explain_en: '선택하다' is you choosing; '선택되다' is having been picked by the one choosing. When a person gets picked, spoken Korean more naturally says '뽑히다'. You often meet it on app screens as the label '선택됨'.

examples.en: I often get compared to my older sister, and it upsets me.
The prices of the two companies can be compared at a glance.

examples.ko: 다른 사람과 비교되면 기분이 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't feel good when I'm compared with others.

examples.ko: 이 두 식당은 맛과 가격이 자주 비교되는 곳이에요.
examples.en: These two restaurants are often compared on taste and price.

examples.ko: 새 영화는 전편과 비교될 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: The new movie can't help being compared with the original.
Children really dislike being compared to their siblings.

explain: '비교하다'는 내가 견주는 것이고, '비교되다'는 견주어지는 쪽이에요. 'A가 B와 비교되다'처럼 '와/과'를 써요. 형제나 친구와 비교되는 일은 기분이 상하기 쉬워서, 한국에서는 '비교하지 마세요'라는 말을 자주 해요.
explain_en: '비교하다' is you comparing; '비교되다' is being the one compared. The pattern is 'A가 B와 비교되다' with '와/과'. Being compared to a sibling or friend easily hurts feelings, so '비교하지 마세요' is a common thing to say in Korea.

examples.ko: 부모님은 딸을 일찍 결혼시키고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: My parents wanted to marry their daughter off early.
Grandma got her eldest grandson married this spring.
After marrying off their son, the house became quiet.

examples.ko: 두 아이를 한꺼번에 결혼시키려면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Marrying off two children at once costs a lot of money.

examples.ko: 저희 부모님은 내년에 누나를 결혼시킬 거예요.
examples.en: My parents are going to marry off my older sister next year.

examples.ko: 자식을 결혼시키는 일은 부모에게 큰 행사예요.
examples.en: Marrying off a child is a big event for parents.

explain: 주어는 보통 부모나 할머니처럼 결혼을 챙기는 어른이에요. '결혼하다'는 본인이 결혼하는 것이고, '결혼시키다'는 어른이 자식을 결혼하게 만드는 것이에요. 딸은 '시집보내다', 아들은 '장가보내다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: The subject is usually an adult who handles the wedding, like a parent or grandmother. '결혼하다' is the person marrying; '결혼시키다' is an adult getting a child married. For a daughter you can also say '시집보내다', and for a son '장가보내다'.

examples.en: I have a lot of work, so things have gotten much harder lately.
Exercising outside gets harder in winter.
As the exam gets closer, studying will get harder.
I didn't give up even as the situation got harder and harder.
Breathing got hard when I climbed the stairs, so I rested.
What if getting to work gets harder after we move?

explain: '힘들다'는 지금의 상태이고, '힘들어지다'는 그 상태로 변해 가는 것이에요. 몸이 지치는 것뿐 아니라 마음이나 상황이 부담스러워질 때도 써요. 반대로 쉬워지면 '편해지다'나 '쉬워지다'를 써요.
explain_en: '힘들다' is the current state; '힘들어지다' is turning into that state. It covers not only a tired body but also a mind or situation becoming a burden. When things ease up, use '편해지다' or '쉬워지다'.

examples.ko: 이 뮤지컬은 매일 저녁 서울에서 공연돼요.
examples.en: This musical is performed in Seoul every evening.
That play was staged in Seoul last month.

examples.ko: 새 콘서트가 다음 달부터 공연될 거예요.
examples.en: The new concert will be performed starting next month.

examples.ko: 공연되는 동안에는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos while it is being performed.

examples.ko: 학교 강당에서 학생 연극이 공연되면 보러 갈래요?
examples.en: If a student play is staged in the school hall, do you want to go see it?

examples.ko: 이 작품은 세계 여러 나라에서 공연되고 있어요.
examples.en: This work is being performed in many countries around the world.

explain: '공연하다'는 무대에서 연주하거나 연기하는 쪽이고, '공연되다'는 작품이 무대에 올라가는 것이에요. 영화는 '상영되다', TV와 라디오는 '방송되다'라고 구분해요. 뮤지컬·연극·콘서트·발레에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '공연하다' is the side performing on stage; '공연되다' is a work being put on stage. Movies are '상영되다', and TV and radio are '방송되다'. It fits musicals, plays, concerts and ballet.

examples.en: Ouch! My finger got caught hard in the door.
Ow, what are you doing stepping on my foot?

examples.ko: 주사를 맞을 때 아야 소리가 나왔어요.
examples.en: I let out an ouch when I got the shot.
My younger sibling fell and cried out ouch.
Ouch, it's so hot! I burned my hand.

examples.ko: 아야, 머리를 세게 부딪쳤는데 괜찮아 보여요?
examples.en: Ow, I hit my head hard. Do I look okay?

explain: 갑자기 아플 때 짧게 나오는 소리예요. 어른은 '아!', '아이고', '아우'도 많이 쓰고, '아야'는 아이들 말 같은 느낌이 조금 있어요. 계속 아픈 것을 설명할 때는 소리 대신 '아파요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the short sound that comes out at a sudden pain. Adults often use '아!', '아이고' or '아우' too, and '아야' has a slightly childlike feel. To explain ongoing pain, use '아파요' instead of the sound.

examples.ko: 이 규칙은 책에 자세히 설명돼 있어요.
examples.en: This rule is explained in detail in the book.
The cause of the accident hasn't been explained yet.

examples.ko: 그 문제는 다음 시간에 설명될 거예요.
examples.en: That problem will be explained next class.

examples.ko: 어려운 말이 쉽게 설명되면 이해하기 편해요.
examples.en: When hard words are explained simply, they're easier to understand.
I tried it following the method that was explained.

examples.ko: 이 단어는 사전에 두 가지로 설명돼요.
examples.en: This word is explained in two ways in the dictionary.

explain: '설명하다'는 내가 알려 주는 것이고, '설명되다'는 글이나 자료에 풀이되어 있는 상태예요. 'A로 설명된다'는 학술적인 글에서 자주 써요. 말할 때는 '설명이 안 돼요'처럼 '설명이 되다'로 풀어서 말하는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: '설명하다' is you explaining; '설명되다' is something being laid out in a text or material. 'A로 설명된다' is common in academic writing. In speech people often split it as '설명이 되다', as in '설명이 안 돼요'.

examples.en: This animal is protected by Korean law.
Personal information is being kept safe.
Our cultural properties must be well protected.

examples.ko: 보호된 숲에서는 나무를 베면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cut trees in a protected forest.
It is dangerous if children are not properly protected.

examples.ko: 이 해변은 바다거북 때문에 보호될 거예요.
examples.en: This beach will be protected because of the sea turtles.

explain: '보호하다'는 지키는 쪽이고, '보호되다'는 지켜지는 상태예요. 법·제도·환경 이야기에 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '지켜지다'가 더 구어적이에요. '보호자'는 아이나 환자를 돌보는 어른을 가리켜요.
explain_en: '보호하다' is the side protecting; '보호되다' is the state of being protected. It appears in talk of laws, systems and the environment, while '지켜지다' is more colloquial. '보호자' refers to the adult looking after a child or a patient.
